selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: After seeing these four truths, what did the traveler become certain about?
questions.answer: He became certain that Allah is One and has no partner.

questions.question: How did this certainty affect his faith?
questions.answer: His faith grew bright and strong.

questions.question: What words did he say with full strength?
questions.answer: He declared that there is no god but Allah, and that Allah is One without any partner.

questions.question: Which four truths are named as signs pointing to Allah’s oneness in this passage?
questions.answer: Absolute Divinity, absolute dominicality, perfections that come from unity, and absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect dominicality with unity?
questions.answer: Because true lordship over everything requires oneness, not shared control.

questions.question: What does the passage say about perfections and unity?
questions.answer: It says those perfections come out of unity.

questions.question: How is sovereignty described in relation to partners?
questions.answer: It is described as something that blocks and opposes any sharing with others.

questions.question: What was the traveler’s final belief after witnessing the four truths mentioned at the start?
questions.answer: He reached clear certainty that Allah is one and without partner.

questions.question: What shows that his belief was not weak or doubtful?
questions.answer: He openly declared it with all his strength.

questions.question: What main lesson is summarized in the brief statement after the traveler’s declaration?
questions.answer: Many great truths in the universe point to Allah’s unity and necessary existence.

questions.question: Which truth in that summary is said to require unity?
questions.answer: Absolute dominicality.

questions.question: Which truth is said to grow out of unity?
questions.answer: Perfections.

questions.question: Which truth is said to prevent any partnership?
questions.answer: Absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: Which of these four is connected with beauty and completeness coming from being one?
questions.answer: Perfections arising from unity.

questions.question: What change took place in the traveler after he observed the four truths?
questions.answer: He reached direct and firm certainty in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What sentence best expresses the traveler’s conclusion?
questions.answer: That only Allah is worthy of worship and He has no partner.

questions.question: Does the passage present Allah’s unity as a guess, a tradition, or a witnessed certainty?
questions.answer: It presents it as a witnessed certainty.

questions.question: What does the phrase about clear witnessing suggest about his faith?
questions.answer: It suggests his faith became very sure and deeply grounded.

questions.question: Name the four realities that are said to point to Allah’s unity.
questions.answer: The manifestation of Divinity, dominicality, perfections from unity, and absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: Which of these four especially shows that sharing divine rule is impossible?
questions.answer: Absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: Why does absolute sovereignty rule out partnership?
questions.answer: Because complete authority does not allow rivals.

questions.question: When the traveler finished reflecting on the four truths, what belief became clear to him?
questions.answer: That Allah alone is God and has no partner.

questions.question: What does the brightening of his faith suggest about his inner state?
questions.answer: It suggests his heart became more confident and enlightened.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the short summary that follows his declaration?
questions.answer: It gathers the main reasons that support Allah’s oneness.
